lines.text: 4.3ForestsofPakistan
The four major types of forests in Pakistan are, coniferous forest, sub-tropical scrub forest,
tropical thornforest (rakh)andmangroves.
Theforests of the various regions of Pakistan differ due to altitude and climate.
ForestofNorthernPakistan
A.Forest of NorthernPakistan/Coniferous
Forest: In the northern mountains, Pine
trees grow due to temperature below
freezing and heavy rainfall.They aremainly
coniferous. They are ever green have
narrow spiky leaves, Seeds in cones or
berries, Usually found in cold climate.
They grow in Gilgit Baltistan, Abbotabad
Mansehra and Swat in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa,
Murree, Rawalpindi in Punjab,Islamabad,
Quetta and Kalat in Balochistan.The main
types of trees are Spruce, Fir and Pine.
·Sub-tropical scrubforest
B. Sub-tropical scrub forests: These forests
grow at loweraltitude, less rainfall and high
temperature.
These are mostly deciduous trees and
scrubs.The deciduous forest have wide flat
leaves and have seeds in the flowers. They
are, not evergreen, and shed their leaves
during autumn season. For example, Oak,
Shisham, Kikar. They grow on the hills and
foothills of lower Himalayas.Sulaiman and
Kirthar ranges, Western mountains,
Peshawar, Waziristan,Kohat and Mardan.
They also grow above the Makran coastal
rangein Balochistan.
